topics.title: The Ice Age That Buried Chicago Under a Mile of Ice
topics.core_question: What did North America actually look like under the Laurentide Ice Sheet, and what happened when it melted?
topics.why_they_click: A sheet of ice a mile thick sat on top of where Chicago, Detroit and New York are today, and the ground you walk on is still rebounding from its weight.
topics.data_source: USGS; NOAA NCEI Paleoclimatology; National Park Service glacial geology resources; peer-reviewed Laurentide Ice Sheet studies
topics.evidence: 'ice age explained' is rising +691% over five years, the strongest search signal on the board, and the backlog has no Laurentide ice-sheet video.

topics.title: The Magnetic Stripes That Proved the Continents Move
topics.core_question: How did a pattern of magnetised stripes on the ocean floor turn continental drift from a joke into accepted fact?
topics.why_they_click: The decisive evidence for plate tectonics was invisible, underwater, and found by accident on a ship's magnetometer tows.
topics.data_source: USGS 'This Dynamic Earth'; NOAA seafloor age and bathymetry datasets; Vine & Matthews 1963 and the peer-reviewed seafloor-spreading literature
topics.evidence: 'plate tectonics explained' is rising +246% over five years, and the backlog covers the consequences of tectonics but never the discovery itself.

topics.title: Doggerland: The Land Britain Lost to the Sea
topics.core_question: How much land did Northwest Europe lose when the ice sheets melted, and who was living on it?
topics.why_they_click: A settled landscape the size of a country now sits under the North Sea, and fishing trawlers keep dragging up the evidence.
topics.data_source: Peer-reviewed Doggerland palaeolandscape studies; British Geological Survey North Sea survey data; NOAA sea-level records
topics.evidence: Rides the same rising 'ice age explained' trend (+691%) while adding a human stake the backlog's ice-age topics don't have.

topics.title: What the Toba Supervolcano Really Did to Humans
topics.core_question: How much did the Toba eruption change the climate and the human story, and how solid is the 'genetic bottleneck' claim?
topics.why_they_click: Toba is taught in some places as the eruption that nearly wiped us out and disputed in the peer-reviewed literature, so the evidence and the argument can both be shown.
topics.data_source: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program; peer-reviewed Toba climate-modelling and archaeological studies
topics.evidence: 'supervolcano' is rising +36% over five years, and the backlog's Yellowstone video busts a myth rather than covering a real VEI 8 eruption.

topics.title: 1964 Alaska: The 9.2 Quake That Shook for 4 Minutes
topics.core_question: What did the second-largest earthquake ever recorded do to Alaska, and why did it rewrite earthquake science?
topics.why_they_click: Four minutes of shaking dropped shorelines by metres, raised others out of the sea, and drowned a town with a tsunami that crossed the Pacific.
topics.data_source: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program; Alaska Earthquake Center (University of Alaska Fairbanks); NOAA tsunami records
topics.evidence: 'biggest earthquake in history' is rising +53% over five years, and this extends the backlog's 1960 Chile topic instead of repeating it.

topics.title: New Madrid 1811: When the Mississippi Ran Backwards
topics.core_question: Why did the middle of the North American plate tear open in 1811 and 1812, and is it still capable of doing it again?
topics.why_they_click: A fault hundreds of kilometres from any plate boundary shook hard enough to be felt in Boston and reportedly reversed the Mississippi's flow.
topics.data_source: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program; peer-reviewed New Madrid seismic zone studies
topics.evidence: Carries the rising 'plate tectonics explained' signal (+246%) into a live scientific argument about intraplate faults.

topics.title: Hunga Tonga 2022: The Eruption That Touched Space
topics.core_question: How did a submarine volcano in Tonga produce the tallest eruption plume and the largest atmospheric explosion ever measured by instruments?
topics.why_they_click: Its pressure wave circled the planet several times and every barometer on Earth recorded it, which makes this the most filmed and best instrumented eruption in history.
topics.data_source: NASA Earth Observatory; Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program; NOAA
topics.evidence: 'supervolcano' is rising +36% over five years, and satellite imagery of the blast gives the channel footage no reconstruction can match.

topics.title: The Younger Dryas: When the Earth Turned Cold Again
topics.core_question: Why did the climate lurch back into near-glacial cold around 12,900 years ago, and what finally ended it?
topics.why_they_click: The planet was warming out of the ice age, then flipped back to freezing for more than a thousand years, and the trigger is still argued over.
topics.data_source: NOAA NCEI Paleoclimatology; NASA Earth Observatory; peer-reviewed Younger Dryas studies
topics.evidence: 'ice age explained' is rising +691%; the cause is genuinely contested, so the video can show scientists disagreeing rather than hide it.

topics.title: Pompeii 79 AD: What Actually Killed the People of Pompeii
topics.core_question: Did the people of Pompeii and Herculaneum die from falling ash, from heat, or from the pyroclastic surge, and what do the deposits say?
topics.why_they_click: The skeletons and the ash layers point in different directions, and settling the argument changed how volcanologists model what pyroclastic flows do to a city.
topics.data_source: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program; peer-reviewed studies of the AD 79 deposits; USGS volcano hazards pages
topics.evidence: No direct trend signal, but it sits exactly on the backlog's eruption-forensics pattern set by Mount St Helens, with the best surviving imagery in the field.

topics.title: The Deepest Place on Earth: 11 Kilometres Down
topics.core_question: What is actually at the bottom of the Mariana Trench, and why is the deepest point on the planet a subduction zone?
topics.why_they_click: The pressure at the bottom is more than a thousand times surface pressure, and the surveys of the exact depth disagree with each other by tens of metres.
topics.data_source: NOAA bathymetric surveys of Challenger Deep; USGS; peer-reviewed Mariana Trench studies
topics.evidence: Extends the rising 'plate tectonics explained' trend (+246%) to the most extreme subduction zone ever measured.
